title: Making lists
summary: Keep many values under one name with a list. Positions, len and in work just like they do on text.

intro.text:
So far every name held **one** value. A **list** holds many values, in order, under one name:

```
temps = [18, 21, 16, 24]
```

Square brackets, with commas between the items. `[]` is an **empty** list.

Good news: you already know how to use it. Lists follow the same position rules as text:

- `temps[0]` is the first item, `temps[-1]` the last
- `len(temps)` counts the **items**: 4
- a position past the end stops the program with an **IndexError**

One difference matters: `in` checks **whole items**. `"Be" in ["Ben", "Cleo"]` is False, because no item is exactly `"Be"`.

A list can hold any kind of value, even a mix: `["tea", 2, 1.5]`. The **cells** panel shows one box per item, with its position underneath.
intro.analogy: A row of numbered lockers with one name over the whole row. Each locker holds one thing, and you open a locker by its number, starting from 0.

quiz.why: Positions start at 0, so position 1 is the second item.
len counts items in a list, not the letters inside them.

quiz.q: A list has 5 items. Which position holds the last one?
quiz.why: Positions go 0 to len - 1, so 0 to 4. -1 works too.
in on a list looks for an item that is exactly "ap". There is none.
+ joins the items of two lists into one new list.

quiz.q: Which of these is an empty list?
quiz.why: [] has no items. [0] and [""] each hold one item, and "" is empty text, not a list.

mistakes.title: Forgetting a comma between items
mistakes.explain: Every item needs a comma before the next one. Python sees 2 and 3 side by side and cannot read the line.

gen.error: SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?

mistakes.title: Using len as the last position
mistakes.explain: len is 3, but the positions are 0, 1 and 2. The last one is len - 1, or simply -1.

gen.error: IndexError: list index out of range

mistakes.title: Adding a number to a list with +
mistakes.explain: + only joins a list to another list. Put the number in brackets so it becomes a list of one item.
